From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Q4 capacity planning — BrightPath (usage + proposed options)

Hi Sanjay / BrightPath procurement team,

Thanks for the heads up on the upcoming renewal window. We ran a focused analysis on BrightPath’s last 90 days and wanted to share a concise set of options so procurement can pick the path that minimizes unit-cost impact while keeping latency SLOs intact. Attached: brightpath-usage-q2-q3.pdf (rolling utilization, 95th/99th token/sec), proposed-slab.xlsx (three priced options).

Quick summary of what we observed:
- Sustained 30-day mean GPU utilization: ~62% (A100-equivalent slot baseline)
- 95th percentile token throughput spiked to 2.8x baseline during three campaign windows (avg duration 3–6 hours)
- KV-cache hit rate for chat workloads averages 28% (opportunity for prefix caching)
- Current burst credits cover ~10% of peak exposure but are near-depleted this month

Options we recommend (each in the attached XLS):
1) Conservative top-up (convert burst -> reserved): +12 A100-equivalent slots, convert 40% of burst to reserved capacity. Minimal price delta.
2) Reslice + quant profile (preferred): +24 A100-equivalent slots, reprofile 30% of existing slots to 8-bit quant profile for non-production inference. This preserves tail latency by routing latency-sensitive requests to hot slots.
3) Aggressive reserve + burst buffer: +32 slots reserved + 2x burst pool, higher commitment but lowest per-token cost.

Ask: can we set a 45-minute call tomorrow to walk procurement through the cost/latency tradeoffs? If you prefer, Ben and Karthik can produce a short 1-pager recommendation with our preferred option and estimated new monthly commit.

Thanks,

Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
(t) +1 415-555-0172

Attachments: brightpath-usage-q2-q3.pdf, proposed-slab.xlsx

Tessa — thanks for this. Helpful to see the utilization breakdown. A couple points from our side:

- The campaign peaks you flagged align with a new feature rollout we did in early June; those are likely to repeat in Q4 unless we throttle client-side sampling.
- Procurement wants to avoid a large overcommit if we can convert existing burst credits to reserved capacity or get a staged commit.

Can you provide a concrete monthly cost delta for option 2 (Reslice + quant profile) vs option 1 for BP-4382? If we can stage the commit (e.g., +24 slots in Oct, evaluate in Jan and then convert the rest) that would be ideal. I’ve attached a preliminary PO draft (po-draft.docx) for internal review.

Team / Sanjay,

I put together a pragmatic reslice that balances BrightPath’s cost targets and the need to keep tail latency under 120ms for chat flows. See attached reslice-proposal.pdf for diagrams and per-slot pricing lines. High-level recommendation (our preferred):

- Add 24 A100-equivalent reserved slots in October (BP-4382 tranche A)
- Reprofile 30% of current fleet to 8-bit quantization (non-prod and low-req paths) -> expected 18–22% cost reduction on those workloads
- Maintain a 12-slot burst pool dedicated to campaign surges; set automatic refill threshold at 65% nominal utilization
- Pricing: incremental commit ~ $42,500/month for tranche A (+24 slots), staged review Jan 15 2028 to consider +8 further slots if utilization persists

Risk notes:
- If BrightPath moves to a multi-model composition with higher KV-cache divergence we may need hot-slot reallocation quickly — add 7-day autoscale window for reprofile rollbacks.
- Short-term KPI: reduce 99th token latency by ~15ms via dedicated burst pool routing.

Action requested from Sales/PD:
- Confirm the go/no-go on +24 Oct tranche by EOD Aug 18 so we can lock pricing and produce a DocuSign SOW.
- Karthik: please confirm the autoscale guardrails we recommended and the estimated lead time to provision the reserved slots (expected 14–21 days).

Ben Carter
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference
